title: [Bounty $1000] Reduce RISCV instructions used to pass on tensix instructions using AI/Optimizer.

The number of tensix instructions to do a particular task can be easily optimized with human thinking, as the main task would have an algorithm and the proper instructions and sequence can often be easily chosen. But to pass on the tensix insturctions to the tensix engine, we often use MOPs and Replay buffers to pass them so that the number of RISCV instructions are rerduced. That part has too many ways of accomplishing and is not too easy to find out what is the most optimal way all the time. 

This is where we can use AI to reduce the number of RISV instructions used, by varying the possibilities of writing the MOP and arrangement of the replay buffer. Overall the task is 

Objective : Minimize the number of RISCV instructions to issue instructions to tensix engine 
Constraints : Sequence of tensix instructions passed remains the same
                       Only specified amount of replay buffer is used (for example if Math thread uses whole of the buffer, it may clash with SFPU algorithms when they are run from a separate thread on WH/BH for the buffer being shared. 
                        Take into account two ways of writing mops and their constraints. 

An AI agent may be asked to do it for all the ops we have and then we filter out the good suggestions and apply them.

comments.body: @vvukomanovicTT  (since you are into AI kernel generation)

Hi @amahmudTT @pmilenkovicTT @fvranicTT @vvukomanovicTT,

Heads up, going to take a swing at this. I've been doing similar work on BarraCUDA (github.com/Zaneham/BarraCUDA), my open-source hobby compiler. The Tenstorrent backend emits RV32IM for the baby cores already and I've been building out the scheduler / optimiser layer, so MOP and replay-buffer minimisation sits in the same problem space.

I'll add a classical optimiser pass that searches MOP layouts and replay arrangements with thread-sharing constraints encoded, verifies functional equivalence of the Tensix stream, and minimises RISCV instruction count. Will prototype on a small set of ops first.

PR coming when I've got something to show. Will post here when it's up.

@Zaneham thanks for volunteering. The llk repo has been merged with tt-metal repo. Any PR has to be against the tt-metal repo.

@jberkowitzTT  is the person assigning the bounties to bounty hunters. @jberkowitzTT could you assign this to Zaneham ?

Absolutely!

Thanks @Zaneham for the interest, and let us know when you have any questions or we can help with anything!

Thanks @Zaneham for the interest, the bounty is now yours! Please update this issue with your progress within 2 weeks. You will have 2 months maximum to complete this bounty, after which it will be reopened.

Review our [Bounty Terms & Conditions](https://docs.tenstorrent.com/bounty_terms.html), as these terms apply. Good luck with the project, and let us know if there are any bugs/issues on our side that are stopping you from completing the bounty. 

If you need access to Tenstorrent hardware, we can provide that for you through the cloud. Please comment asking for access once you've been assigned to the bounty if you need access.

Let me know if you have any other questions or if we can help!

Just a wee progress update.

Got the replay-buffer half of the optimiser going. I built it verifier-first, so every arrangement it suggests gets checked against the exact Tensix stream before it's allowed to count. Keeps me honest on the "same instructions out" constraint rather than just trusting myself.

So far it'll:
- spot repeated instruction blocks, load each into the replay buffer once (executing the first pass as it loads), then replay it everywhere it shows up again. Copes with a few different blocks at once, not just one.
- stay inside a buffer budget, so it won't hand you a plan that stomps on slots another thread needs. That's the Math/SFPU sharing thing from the issue. Tell it 16 slots and it behaves.
- spit out an actual do-this suggestion by offset: "record these N instructions into slots [a,b), replay there instead of those."

Gave it a real kernel to chew on: pulled the MVMUL inner block out of `llk_math_matmul.h` (non-transposed path), 15 instructions, and it folds the repeated 7-instruction run into a load plus a replay. 15 down to 10 RISC-V issues, call it a third off, and verified to come back as the identical Tensix stream. In sim mind you, not on a chip yet. I checked the execute-while-loading behaviour against `load_replay_buf` so that first-pass-as-the-load bit isn't a guess.

It's sitting on top of my open Tensix assembler (github.com/Zaneham/ttas), second piece of a toolchain I'm building out.

Where I've hit a wall, and it's the MOP half: I can't work out from the headers whether the double-loop MOP expander (`ckernel_template`) actually issues the NOP template slots, the `start_op`, the `end_op`s, an unused second loop op, or whether it just skips the NOPs. That one detail decides whether a MOP can reproduce a clean repeated stream at all, so it's holding up the whole MOP-fitting pass. If someone knows off the top of their head, that'd unblock me on the spot, no hardware needed for that one.

Separately on hardware: the Koyeb access is a known issue at the moment. I've had a go at getting it working and emailed their support, but no joy yet. So if there's another route onto a chip in the meantime I'd jump on it, just to run the optimiser's output end to end and confirm it holds up.

Cheers

@mcraigheadTT If you know the answer to the above question could you drop a line here ? From the ISA doc it seems the nops are not executed.

Hi, I can take a look, as the exact NOP behavior for MOP (which NOPs does it emit vs. which NOPs does it swallow) has been on my list of "need to understand better" for a while now. In addition to the doc there - @Zaneham , you may find it helpful to look at the MOP code in https://github.com/tenstorrent/ttsim/blob/main/src/tensix.cpp. It's essentially the same as the ISA doc, but the ISA doc being written in what I would call "pseudo-Python" for MOP (async, yield) is a bit hairy.
I'm digging into this now; some minor ISA spec updates forthcoming, but I doubt they will substantively change the conclusions in your specific cases w.r.t. when a NOP is emitted vs. when it isn't.
Finished ISA spec review and made minor edits based on my findings: https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-isa-documentation/commit/9ba1ce0ad519b2c83e5465528ae6cc237ba53560

Oh beauty, update time, and a massive thanks first.

@amahmudTT  @mcraigheadTT you legends. The NOP thing was the one wall holding up the entire MOP half and you just
sorted it. @mcraigheadTT going and actually reviewing the ISA spec over a question from some random on the internet,
that's properly above and beyond. The double-loop expander matches the documented behaviour now: NOP slots skipped,
one op per inner step, the alternation doubling the count, last step replacing instead of appending. My first crack at
it was quietly wrong in a way my own tests waltzed straight past, so the timing was perfect.

And the ttsim tip, mean. Yanked the mop/replay expander out of tensix.cpp and turned it into an oracle, so now I fuzz
my own expander against it a few thousand plans a run. If they ever disagree, ttsim wins every time, cause it's yours
and I'm just some bloke. Way better net than my hand-written tests, and it means I can trust the thing without a chip
in the loop, so the Koyeb gremlins haven't actually held me up.

Matmul's the fun bit. I can model the real config the way you actually program it now, record the block then a MOP
whose body replays it, expanded properly. Chuck the raw stream at the optimiser with zero hints and it lands on the
exact same record-once-replay trick the kernel hand-codes. 64 issues down to 20, verified, real MVMUL encodings. Sim
still, but the encodings are legit.

Replay and MOP are one pass now, grabs whichever's cheaper per chunk. Still building it out. More soon. Cheers team,
genuinely good fun this one.

Glad it was helpful! I cannot promise that the spec or ttsim code are 100% bug free, but I did quite a bit of analysis of this logic vs. the WH and BH RTL and I am not aware of any discrepancies at this point. We will continue scrubbing these specs and simulator code over time.

Meatier update this time, and thanks again for the NOP answer, that's what got the MOP half unstuck.

On approach: the issue floats an AI agent generating suggestions to filter, and I went deliberately the other way, a deterministic search with a verifier in front of it rather than an LLM. For this problem a plausible-but-wrong arrangement is worse than none, an off-by-one replay offset or a wrong loop count looks completely reasonable and only bites on silicon. So every arrangement the tool proposes gets expanded back into the exact Tensix stream and checked word-for-word against the original before it's allowed to count, and the expander itself is fuzzed against ttsim so it can't quietly lie to me. Net effect: nothing incorrect comes out, so there's no "filter the good ones" step to do. It handles both MOP templates, the replay buffer, execute-while-loading, and the Math/SFPU shared-buffer budget. Code's here if you fancy a poke around: https://github.com/Zaneham/tt-mop

Honest finding from reading the LLK though: your ops are already tuned really well. transpose_dest especially is gorgeous, recording one buffer and composing the unpack template out of overlapping replay sub-ranges isn't something I'd improve on. matmul does record-once-loop, reduce wraps its pool loop. Run the tool over the matmul stream and it lands independently on the same record-once-replay arrangement you'd hand-coded, which is a nice confirmation but, well, a confirmation, not a saving.

So before I grind it over all fifteen and report a pile of "yep, already optimal", I'd rather point it where there's real surface. Where do you reckon the headroom is? A few guesses: newer ops that haven't had the transpose_dest treatment, whole fused kernels rather than single ops (per-op tuning can't see repetition that spans op boundaries, an automated pass can), or the Blackhole variants. Happy to aim it wherever's most useful.

Cheers.

@Zaneham A whole lot of quasar ops are being written but they are mostly ported from BH and WH, they could be good candidates, but is there any documentation of the way how the quasar ops uses replay buffer and mops @rtawfik01 or are they all the same as before ?

@Zaneham even if no op sees any improvement, a documented procedure of how the tool is "BUILT & Used" so that with some reading any member of our team can replicate the effort and appy on future ops, should also be okay. And thanks a lot for analyzing, the confirmation is great too. Thanks !

And is putting the ability of use overlapping portions of the replay buffer and optimize the replay buffer as you mentioned for is being done for transpose_dest, can be modeled by your tool ?
@amahmudTT @jberkowitzTT If @Zaneham is no longer working on this issue, I'd be glad to work on it if you could assign it to me. Thank you!

There is a PR ready for review at https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-metal/pull/49170

Kind regards,

Zane
